rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: One card is drawn at random from a well shuffled deck of 52 playing cards. The probability that it is a red ace card, is :
rows.solution:
A deck has 2 red aces (hearts and diamonds) among 52 cards.

\(P(\text{red ace}) = \dfrac{2}{52} = \dfrac{1}{26}\), which is option (B) \(\dfrac{1}{26}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: Solve the following system of linear equations algebraically : \(2x + 5y = -4\); \(4x - 3y = 5\)
rows.solution:
\(2x + 5y = -4\) ... (i)

\(4x - 3y = 5\) ... (ii)

Multiply (i) by 2: \(4x + 10y = -8\). Subtracting (ii) from this, \(13y = -13\), so \(y = -1\). Then \(2x - 5 = -4\), so \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Verification: \(2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 5(-1) = -4\) and \(4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 3(-1) = 5\). Both equations are satisfied.

\(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(y = -1\).

rows.stem: In \(\Delta ABC\), altitudes AD and BE are drawn. If AD = 7 cm, BE = 9 cm and EC = 12 cm then, find the length of CD.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - triangle ABC with altitude AD to BC and altitude BE to AC, right angles marked at D and E; the stem states every fact used (D on BC and E on AC follow from 'altitudes AD and BE'). Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
In triangles BEC and ADC: \(\angle BEC = \angle ADC = 90^\circ\) (BE and AD are altitudes) and \(\angle C\) is common. So \(\Delta BEC \sim \Delta ADC\) (AA similarity).

Corresponding sides are proportional: \(\dfrac{BE}{AD} = \dfrac{EC}{DC}\), so \(\dfrac{9}{7} = \dfrac{12}{CD}\).

\(CD = \dfrac{12 \times 7}{9} = \dfrac{28}{3}\) cm \(\approx 9.33\) cm.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: The sum of the digits of a 2-digit number is 14. The number obtained by interchanging its digits exceeds the given number by 18. Find the number.
rows.solution:
Let the tens digit be x and the units digit y, so the number is \(10x + y\).

Sum of the digits: \(x + y = 14\) ... (i)

Interchanging the digits gives \(10y + x\), so \(10y + x = 10x + y + 18\), that is \(9y - 9x = 18\), or \(y - x = 2\) ... (ii)

Adding (i) and (ii): \(2y = 16\), so \(y = 8\), and then \(x = 6\).

The number is 68. (Check: \(6 + 8 = 14\) and \(86 - 68 = 18\).)

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: The inner and outer radii of a hollow cylinder surmounted on a hollow hemisphere of same radii are 3 cm and 4 cm respectively. If height of the cylinder is 14 cm, then find its total surface area (inner and outer).
rows.solution:
The vessel has an inner surface (radius 3 cm), an outer surface (radius 4 cm) and a flat ring at the open top joining them. Each surface is a cylinder of height 14 cm on a hemisphere, so its curved area is \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi r(r + h)\).

Inner surface \(= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 3 \times (3 + 14) = \dfrac{2244}{7}\) cm\(^2\).

Outer surface \(= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 4 \times (4 + 14) = \dfrac{3168}{7}\) cm\(^2\).

Area of the ring \(= \pi(4^2 - 3^2) = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 = 22\) cm\(^2\).

Total surface area \(= \dfrac{2244}{7} + \dfrac{3168}{7} + 22 = \dfrac{5412 + 154}{7} = \dfrac{5566}{7} \approx 795.14\) cm\(^2\).

rows.stem: From the top of a 15 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is found to be \(30^\circ\). From the bottom of the same building, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be \(60^\circ\). Find the height of the tower and the distance between tower and the building.
rows.solution:
Let CD be the building (15 m) and AB the tower, with C and A on the ground, \(CA = x\) m. Draw DE perpendicular to AB, so that \(DE = x\) m and \(AE = 15\) m; let \(BE = h\) m.

From D, the angle of elevation of B is \(30^\circ\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{BE}{DE}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h}{x}\) and \(x = \sqrt{3}\,h\) ... (i)

From C, the angle of elevation of B is \(60^\circ\): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{CA}\), so \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{h + 15}{x}\) and \(h + 15 = \sqrt{3}\,x\) ... (ii)

Substituting (i) in (ii): \(h + 15 = \sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}\,h = 3h\), so \(h = \dfrac{15}{2} = 7.5\) m, and \(x = 7.5\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{2}\) m.

The height of the tower is \(7.5 + 15 = 22.5\) m, and the distance between the tower and the building is \(\dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{2}\) m \(\approx 12.99\) m.

rows.stem:
In the given figure, diameters AC and BD of the circle intersect at O. If \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\) and OA = 10 cm, then :

(i) find the length of the chord AB.

(ii) find the area of shaded region.

(Take \(\pi = 3.14\) and \(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\))
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the shaded region is defined only by the drawing: the minor segment APB cut off by chord AB (P on the arc) together with the sector OBC between radius OB, radius OC and the arc BC; the 60 degree angle AOB is marked at O. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
(i) \(OA = OB = 10\) cm (radii) and \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\), so the base angles of triangle OAB are each \(60^\circ\) too. Triangle OAB is equilateral, and \(AB = OA = 10\) cm.

(ii) The shaded region is the minor segment APB together with the sector OBC.

Area of segment APB \(=\) area of sector OAB \(-\) area of triangle OAB \(= 3.14 \times 100 \times \dfrac{60}{360} - \dfrac{1.73}{4} \times 100 = 52.33 - 43.25 = 9.08\) cm\(^2\) (approx.).

AC is a diameter, so \(\angle BOC = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).

Area of sector OBC \(= 3.14 \times 100 \times \dfrac{120}{360} = 104.67\) cm\(^2\) (approx.).

Area of the shaded region \(= 9.08 + 104.67 = 113.75\) cm\(^2\) (approx.).
